name: The Island
text:
1
The Island
10 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island.

This means at least one of these three things is true:

I don't understand why the right answer is right.

I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.

I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.

At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two. 

If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island. 

Fill in your Wrong Answer Journal with the new information you've learned now that the question has canoed away.

Click here to go to The Island (scroll to the bottom!)

name: Thunderdome
text:
2
Thunderdome
30 MINUTES
Instructions

NOTE: Thunderdomes are advanced workouts for those who have plateaued. Beginners can make good progress with other workouts before attempting a Thunderdome.

For each stimulus in the section*, write or speak out each and every one of the following outputs, according to the stimulus type, without looking at the question stem or answer choices:

On an Argument, write or speak your own:

Weaken correct answer

Strengthen correct answer

Necessary assumption

Sufficient assumption

Method correct answer

Argument parts identifications

Parallel Skeleton

Parallel correct answer

Use your favorite topic as a consistent analogous base

This means all your Parallel correct answers can be about dogs or cars across all the questions in the section.

On a Debate, write or speak your own:

Controversy

Agreement

Loophole in both speakers

On a Paradox, write or speak your own:

Resolution

Inference

Contradiction

On a Premise Set, write or speak your own:

Three Inferences

Contradiction

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Translation + CLIR Drill
text:
3
Translation + CLIR Drill
1 SECTION
Instructions

Start a stopwatch.

Read and translate the stimulus* out loud in chunks.

Quip each chunk of the stimulus after you translate.

Continue this process on every stimulus chunk until you reach the end of stimulus.

Immediately proceed to the CLIR after your final quip of the stimulus (or the final quip is the CLIR).

Stop the stopwatch and record your time.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Test-Day Timing Marathon
text:
4
Test-Day Timing Marathon
8 SECTIONS
Instructions

Complete six to eight test-day timed LR sections* in one sitting with no breaks, or complete six to eight test-day timed RC sections in one sitting with no breaks.

This means you should use test-day timing on all sections, not Marathon timing.

Immediately proceed to the next section in the Marathon as soon as the test-day timer expires.

Any questions left unanswered within time will be marked wrong.

NOTE: You can modify the Test-Day Timing Marathon to alternate between LR and RC sections, as you would in a Mixed Section Marathon. Just flip a coin (or ask your favorite digital assistant to flip a coin) to decide each section when you're ready to begin that section mid-Marathon.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Camo Review
text:
5
Camo Review
Instructions

When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.

Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.

At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.

Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.

This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.

Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.

Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.

Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.

Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.

Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

SEE FULL WORKOUT DETAILS

name: Wrong Answer Journal
text:
6
Wrong Answer Journal
Instructions

After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.

For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.

This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.

Fill in your Reason Missed column

In this column, write down what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question.

Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.

The first word of every entry in this column should be "I." 

Example: "I misidentified the question stem."

This will force you to reflect on what you did that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.

Fill in your Solution column

In this column, write down what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again.

Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"

The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..." 

Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."

Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click here to go to your Wrong Answer Journal
